fields.Name: rasa
fields.Description: rasa.io newsletter and audience-engagement platform. Syncs subscribers (persons and their actions, topics, sends and attributes), newsletter content (posts, content pool, communities) and the v2 messaging/list surface via the rasa.io REST API.

Configuration.AuthFlowNote: v1 (primary/documented target of the current build): step 1 = POST /v1/tokens with an HTTP Basic Authorization header (username:password) plus a JSON body { key: <apiKey> } (definitions.TokenCreateBody, required: [key]); response 201 returns definitions.ApiResonseTokenCreated -> results[].{'rasa-token'} (definitions.RasaToken, format: jwt-token). Step 2 = every subsequent request presents that JWT as a custom header named 'rasa-token' (NOT 'Authorization: Bearer'), per securityDefinitions.authorizer (type: apiKey, name: 'rasa-token', in: header) and the 'send your session token received from the token endpoint' parameter description repeated on every documented v1 operation (e.g. GET /persons). v2 documents a DIFFERENT mechanic for the same path shape (POST /v2/tokens, described as an 'OAuth2 Client Credentials grant' taking grant_type/client_id/client_secret in the body and returning access_token/token_type/expires_in), while its securityDefinitions.RasaToken still names the runtime header 'rasa-token' described as carrying 'JWT token obtained from POST /v2/tokens' — this is an internal inconsistency in the v2 spec (client-credentials response shape vs. an apiKey/rasa-token securityDefinition) and is recorded as a residual doubt, not silently resolved.
Configuration.AuthHeaderPatternNote: Confirmed on GET /persons (v1) parameter: { name: 'rasa-token', in: 'header', required: true, description: 'send your session token received from the token endpoint' } and identically named/placed on every other documented v1 operation. This is NOT the 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' pattern despite the token being JWT-formatted.

v2.note: account_guid / X-Account-GUID super-user scoping is a rasa.io v2-specific multi-account mechanic, not a general OAuth2 feature.

PaginationDefaults.typeNote: Both versions use skip/limit query params (offset pagination), NOT a true opaque cursor -- e.g. v1 GET /persons parameters include { name: 'skip', type: integer, minimum: 0 } and { name: 'limit', type: integer, minimum: 0, maximum: 50 }; v2 GET /contacts has { name: 'skip', default: 0 } and { name: 'limit', default: 50 } (no vendor-stated maximum field on limit itself, but its description states 'max 5000'). A response-metadata envelope (v1 PersonsApiResponseMetadata.next_link / InsightApiResponseMetadata.next_link; v2 ResponseMetadata) additionally carries a next_link URL plus record_count/total_query_count to drive the loop -- so the connector should follow next_link when present rather than hand-incrementing skip.

IncrementalSyncCapability.supportedNote: Supported per-endpoint, NOT uniformly -- confirmed by direct parameter enumeration, not assumed.
IncrementalSyncCapability.primaryWatermarkFieldNote: GET /persons (v1) documents FOUR watermark query params: created_since, created_before, updated_since, updated_before (rasa-v1-openapi.json paths./persons.get.parameters). For a true incremental sync (catching field updates, not just new rows), updated_since is the correct primary watermark; created_since alone would miss updates to existing persons.
IncrementalSyncCapability.perObjectException_insightsActions: GET /insights/actions documents only created_since/created_before (no updated_since) -- confirmed via direct parameter enumeration of paths['/insights/actions'].get.parameters in rasa-v1-openapi.json. Matches the Cimatri client's live-integration example exactly (SOURCES.json crossCheck).
IncrementalSyncCapability.perObjectException_insightsTopics: GET /insights/topics documents NO filter/watermark params at all besides the required rasa-token header -- every pull is a full re-fetch; no incremental sync is possible for this object per the machine spec.
IncrementalSyncCapability.perObjectException_analytics: GET /analytics/{activities,articles,images,topics} use a wholly different filtering vocabulary (date_range / start_date / end_date / interval query params, not created_since/updated_since) -- confirmed by direct parameter enumeration.
IncrementalSyncCapability.perObjectException_personSubResources: GET /persons/{id}/{actions,topics,sends,attributes} (nested-under-person) document NO filter or pagination params whatsoever -- they return the full un-paged child set for one person.

Configuration.APIVersioningStrategyNote: Two independent, non-migrating API generations are both live and documented side by side: v1 at host api.rasa.io, basePath /v1 (rasa-v1-openapi.json: host='api.rasa.io', basePath='/v1'); v2 at the same host, basePath /v2 (rasa-v2-openapi.json: host='api.rasa.io', basePath='/v2'). The version segment is embedded directly in the URL path, not a header or accept-header. v1 has NO Person/Insights/Analytics/Posts-in-v2-shape equivalent and v2 has NO List/Newsletter/Blast/Sequence/Subscription-in-v1-shape equivalent -- a connector must pick a version per object family, not treat v2 as 'v1 plus more endpoints.'

universalPK.note: Every top-level v1 resource inspected declares its primary key as a UUID-formatted string named 'id' -- e.g. PersonsApiGetResponseItem.id: { type: string, format: uuid, example: 'd290f1ee-6c54-4b01-90e6-d701748f0851' } (rasa-v1-openapi.json). This is a vendor-wide convention for top-level v1 resources; several v1 child/aggregate objects instead use COMPOSITE keys with no single 'id' field (e.g. Insight Topic Score keyed on person_id+topic per the 1.1.x prior baseline, Analytics Activity keyed on bucket_start+metric_name) -- 'id' is the default single-PK convention, not a guarantee every object has one. v2 Contact objects also use a GUID-formatted id ('Contact GUID' per the DELETE /contacts/{id} path parameter description in rasa-v2-openapi.json), consistent with the same convention.

Configuration.WebhooksAvailableNote: No 'webhook' term (case-insensitive) appears anywhere in either rasa-v1-openapi.json or rasa-v2-openapi.json (confirmed via grep -io 'webhook' against both raw spec files -- zero matches), and neither spec documents any push/callback-registration path or tag. Absence is evidenced by exhaustive search of the only two machine-readable sources, not assumed.
Configuration.BulkOperationsAvailableNote: v2 documents POST /contacts/bulk ('Create contacts in bulk', tag: contacts) in rasa-v2-openapi.json. No equivalent bulk-write endpoint exists in the v1 spec (v1 POST /persons is 'adds persons' -- singular add per the OAS summary; PUT /persons is 'update persons' but was not confirmed to accept an array body in this pass, see gaps). BulkOperationsAvailable therefore reflects v2's /contacts/bulk specifically.

Configuration.ConcurrencyControlNote: Not provable from either spec: no ETag / If-Match / If-Unmodified-Since header, no version/revision field, and no optimistic-lock response code (409/412) is documented on any write operation in rasa-v1-openapi.json or rasa-v2-openapi.json. Left UNSET per the provable-only rule rather than defaulted to 'none' as a guess -- 'none' is itself a claim (the vendor definitively lacks the capability) this pass cannot make from docs alone; a live credentialed conflict-write probe would be needed to confirm no 409/412 exists in practice.

Person.evidence: DELETE /persons/{id} description: 'Deletes a person by id - this is an undoable action, and should be reserved for uses such as GDPR deletion. This is not the action to use for normal de-activation of subscribed members.' (rasa-v1-openapi.json). GET /persons/deleted ('List archived (deleted) persons as tombstones') independently confirms an archive/tombstone model exists: 'Returns minimal {id, archived_date} tombstones for community persons archived on or after archived_since ... archived_date is currently approximated by the person's updated timestamp.'

(rasa-v2-openapi.json). GET /contacts/deleted exists as the v2 tombstone-reconciliation feed (per SOURCE_STUDY.md TaxonomyLeaves #22 'Deleted/Removed Contact').

DeleteSemantics.note: Both version generations converge on soft-delete/archive as the primary, vendor-recommended pattern for normal record removal, with tombstone-reconciliation feeds (GET /persons/deleted, GET /contacts/deleted) to detect archived rows on pull. v1 additionally exposes a separate hard-delete path scoped explicitly to GDPR erasure requests.

Configuration.DefaultSyncDirectionNote: Per standing discipline, every object defaults to Pull (read-only) regardless of documented write capability. Bidirectional is opt-in and is NOT recommended as a default for any rasa.io object in this pass -- see METADATA_REPORT preconditions.
Configuration.DefaultConflictResolutionNote: Left UNSET. No ConcurrencyControl signal (ETag/version) is documented (see ConcurrencyControlNote), so 'MostRecent' cannot be justified per the framework rule ('no ETag/version ⇒ don't recommend MostRecent'). Should bidirectional ever be enabled, a snapshot-3-way or SourceWins/DestWins policy chosen per-object at that time is the safer default than guessing here.

Configuration.ScopeReason: scopeOfInterest = union(29 doc-coverable leaves, prior-1.1.x 8-object surface) minus nothing — no member of either set is provably non-existent, so the union is exactly the 29 doc leaves. The prior 8 are a strict SUBSET of the 29 and every one is retained, so there is no shrink for RegressionDiff to justify: persons->Person, posts->Post, insights-actions->Insight Action, insights-topics->Insight Topic, person-attributes->Person Attribute, analytics-activities->Analytics Activity, analytics-articles->Analytics Article, analytics-topics->Analytics Topic.
